summary.en: Use the **past simple** for finished actions and events in order: _I opened the door and saw a parcel._ Use the **past continuous** for the background, an action in progress at a past moment, or a longer action interrupted by a shorter one: _I was cooking when the lights went out._
summary.es: Se parece a la pareja «pretérito indefinido / imperfecto», pero no es igual: el past continuous solo se usa para acciones en curso en un momento pasado, no para hábitos (para eso: past simple o used to).

form: Past simple: subject + past form (**opened**, **saw**); questions and negatives with **did**
Linking words: **when** (usually + past simple), **while** and **as** (usually + past continuous)
State verbs (_know_, _want_, _believe_) normally stay in the past simple

uses.text: **A sequence of finished actions** → past simple: _She **picked up** her bag, **locked** the door and **left**._
**An action in progress at a moment** → past continuous: _At eight o'clock I **was queuing** at the bank._
**A long action interrupted** → past continuous + past simple: _He **was driving** home when his phone **rang**._

note.en: The longer action is the background; the short one is the event.
note.es: La acción larga es el fondo; la corta es el suceso que la interrumpe.

uses.text: **Two actions at the same time** → past continuous with _while_: _While she **was cooking**, he **was setting** the table._
**Scene-setting** in a story: _It **was raining** and people **were hurrying** along the street._

mistakes.wrong: When I was arriving, the manager said hello.
mistakes.right: When I arrived, the manager said hello.

why.en: A short, completed action (arrive) takes the past simple, not the continuous.
why.es: Una acción puntual y terminada va en past simple.

mistakes.wrong: When I was a child, I was playing in the street every day.
mistakes.right: When I was a child, I played in the street every day.

why.en: A repeated habit in the past is not an action in progress, so use the past simple (or used to).
why.es: Un hábito pasado no es «en curso»: past simple o used to.

mistakes.wrong: I was wanting a coffee, so I stopped at the café.
mistakes.right: I wanted a coffee, so I stopped at the café.

why.en: Want is a state verb and is not normally used in the continuous.
why.es: Want es un verbo de estado: no suele llevar -ing.

examples.en: I was waiting for the bus when I noticed my wallet was missing.
examples.es: Estaba esperando el autobús cuando me di cuenta de que no tenía la cartera.

examples.en: We watched the news and then went to bed.
examples.es: Vimos las noticias y luego nos acostamos.

examples.en: What were you doing at ten o'clock last night?
The students were chatting while the teacher was setting up the projector.
I fell asleep while I was reading on the train.
It was snowing heavily, so the match was cancelled.
She didn't hear the alarm because she was wearing headphones.
As we were leaving the cinema, it started to rain.
He lost his keys on Friday and found them on Monday.

practice.prompt: I ___ along the High Street when I met my old teacher.

explanation.en: The walking was in progress when the meeting interrupted it.

practice.prompt: She ___ the email, closed her laptop and went home.

explanation.en: A sequence of finished actions takes the past simple.

practice.prompt: While we ___ dinner, the power went off.

explanation.en: While introduces the longer action in progress: past continuous.

practice.prompt: The film ___ at 8.30, so we were late for the start.

explanation.en: A single event at a fixed time takes the past simple.
